name: Helmet
label: AmRep
lede: Page Hamilton left Band of Susans, started a band with short hair and no solos, and cut a $2,500 record that kept Amphetamine Reptile going through the 1990s. Interscope won the bidding war, Meantime went gold, and after the 1998 split Hamilton brought the name back in 2004 and hasn't put it down.

eras.title: Short hair, no solos, one Minneapolis label
eras.text: Hamilton leaves Band of Susans and starts a New York band with no solos in it. Tom Hazelmyer hears it, signs it to Amphetamine Reptile, and a 1990 record made for $2,500 helps keep the label open for the decade.

years.h: Page Hamilton leaves Band of Susans to start Helmet
years.p: Hamilton, who came up around [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]]'s guitar ensembles, forms the band in New York with bassist [[Henry Bogdan|1b854c5b-5b07-4c1d-b5ad-61abe484e1f1]], guitarist [[Peter Mengede|b2d7a5e6-c790-4e17-b413-9e4d2f9d225a]] and drummer [[John Stanier|4d81d3a6-b6f2-42ba-b93c-348b73097080]].

years.h: Helmet started out as "Helmuth"
years.p: Mengede's then-wife Reyne suggested the Germanic name. Hamilton heard the thing you wear on your head and kept the English spelling.
years.xp: Hamilton thought it "sounded like a pretty cool name for a band." The names that lost: Cry Ruth, Poly Orchids, Tuna Lorenzo and Froth Albumen.

years.src: Wikipedia: Amphetamine Reptile Records · Wikipedia: Helmet (band)
years.h: Amphetamine Reptile puts out "Born Annoying"
years.p: Label founder [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]], who also plays guitar in Halo of Flies, releases Helmet's first single, a 7-inch, in late 1989.
years.xp: Hazelmyer started Amphetamine Reptile Records in 1986 to release his own band, and later moved it from Washington state to Minneapolis. "Born Annoying" came out again in 1995 on an album of the same name, with extra tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Strap It On · Wikipedia: Amphetamine Reptile Records · Kerrang!: The great unsung
years.h: Strap It On costs $2,500 and keeps a label open
years.p: Cut at Fun City in New York with Wharton Tiers and out in October on Amphetamine Reptile: stop-start riffs, no solos, about half an hour.
years.xp:
Hazelmyer said the record "helped support the other things that sold less" on AmRep. It had sold about 10,000 copies by September 1992 and 40,000 by February 1995. Interscope reissued it in January 1993.

Alternative Press ranked it No. 12 in its 1998 list of the 90 greatest albums of the '90s. Deftones covered Sinatra on their 2005 collection B-Sides & Rarities. Kerrang! called the record "an ugly beast indeed."

years.h: A 1990 night at CBGB, kept on tape
years.p: The band's 1990 CBGB set came out in 2021 on the archive collection Live and Rare.

eras.title: The auction after Nirvana
eras.text: Every label wants a loud guitar band from the underground. Interscope wins the bidding, and Meantime goes gold on the strength of a video Beavis and Butt-Head had opinions about.

years.cap: Helmet's four-man line-up on a stairwell, around 1992
years.h: Interscope outbids the field for Helmet
years.p: After Nirvana, labels hunt the underground for loud guitar bands. Interscope signs Helmet for three albums, with an unusual amount of creative control.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the deal at a $1.2 million advance split across three records, $400,000 each, plus $50,000 in tour support. The Meantime page says approximately $1 million, so the exact figure isn't settled.

Amphetamine Reptile kept the vinyl rights.

years.h: Albini takes the title track, Tiers the rest
years.p: Meantime is cut between December 1991 and February 1992 for $25,000: Wharton Tiers at Fun City in New York, [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] on "In the Meantime" at CRC in Chicago, [[Andy Wallace|665695c1-d546-4141-8dd7-1cd40a1eea71]] on the mix.
years.xp: Helmet produced it themselves. Wikipedia has the drum parts for one song done in "an hour and a half or so of a morning."

yt: Full set at Cabaret Metro, Chicago, 1992
years.h: Interscope's first Helmet record slips from April to June 23
years.p: Pushed back from April, Meantime reaches No. 1 on the Heatseekers chart and No. 68 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Three singles got videos: Unsung, In the Meantime (June 8, 1992) and Give It. It went gold in 1994, the only Helmet album that has, and Wikipedia says it has sold over two million copies worldwide.

The cover is David Plowden's 1979 photograph of a puddler in a blast furnace cast house at a steel mill in East Chicago, Indiana. The record shipped in two reversible covers, red and blue. Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 54 on its 100 greatest metal albums.

yt: "Unsung", the video Beavis and Butt-Head watch
years.h: Beavis and Butt-Head watch Helmet's "Unsung" video
years.p: The two keep going: "If you, like, saw these guys on the street, you wouldn't even know they were cool."
years.xp: The band had turned down metal's usual look for t-shirts, jeans, sneakers and short haircuts, and the cartoon noticed. Unsung was the first of the three Meantime videos.

years.h: Interscope gives Strap It On a second release
years.p: The 1990 debut comes out again in January 1993, so anyone who bought Meantime can go back to the start.

q: Money kind of came in and changed things.
years.h: Peter Mengede leaves over the contract and joins Handsome
years.p: The second guitarist goes in early 1993 after contractual disputes. Handsome's one album comes out on Epic in 1997.
years.xp: Asked about the classic line-up falling apart, Hamilton has pointed at the new money in the room.

years.h: Rob Echeverria, of Rest in Pieces, takes the second guitar
years.p: [[Rob Echeverria|0b8b2179-3147-4736-acbf-8e44d75d1557]] steps into Mengede's spot for the Betty cycle.

years.h: Helmet and House of Pain share a track on Judgment Night
years.p: "Just Another Victim" is one of the rock-meets-rap pairings built for the 1993 film's soundtrack.

eras.title: Jazz chords, a crow movie
eras.text: With the pressure on, Hamilton writes Betty with jazz and blues chords in it. Interscope's push fades, but "Milquetoast" ends up on the soundtrack to The Crow.

years.src: Wikipedia: Betty (Helmet album) · Kerrang!: The great unsung
years.h: Betty peaks at No. 45, with jazz chords in the riffs
years.p: Made at three New York studios with T-Ray and [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]]. An alternate take of "Milquetoast", spelled "Milktoast", lands on The Crow soundtrack before the album is out.
years.xp:
Hamilton on the jazz and blues detours: "I know a lot of fans were disappointed, but I think it's important to try to grow musically." He called those parts his indulgences.

Reviews were mixed at first (AllMusic gave it 3 of 5). It had sold about 500,000 copies worldwide by 1997, 252,000 of them in the US. Rolling Stone put it on a 2014 list of the 40 best records from 1994.

years.h: Helmet plays Black Sabbath in The Jerky Boys
years.p: They cover "Symptom of the Universe" on screen, with Ozzy Osbourne in a cameo as their manager.

years.h: Echeverria leaves on good terms for Biohazard
years.p: A friendlier exit than Mengede's. He goes to [[Biohazard|be5fe2ab-007c-4610-8d53-d81675d06a09]] after the Betty tour, and Hamilton plays the guitar on the next record alone.

eras.title: Down to a trio
eras.text: Helmet finishes Aftertaste as three players, throws out the first mix and tours with the new nu-metal bands. Then the original run ends.

years.h: Helmet throw out the Aftertaste mix and start over
years.p: Dave Sardy's mix is withdrawn after press has already started; Terry Date remixes it, and "Renovation" gets added along the way.
years.xp:
The record was nearly done in late 1996, with interviews done and advance tapes out to journalists. A Canadian bootleg then leaked five weeks before release, which Hamilton estimated cost about 10,000 sales.

It debuted at No. 47 on the Billboard 200 and had sold 132,000 copies by 2004. It was the last album by Hamilton, Bogdan and Stanier together.

years.h: Chris Traynor joins on guitar for the Aftertaste tour
years.p: [[Chris Traynor|80f36457-d56f-4444-a750-cc52bfb77f00]] of Orange 9mm joins on guitar for a tour that opens with Korn and Limp Bizkit in March and runs with the Melvins from July.
years.xp: The tour ran from March to December 10, 1997, with Coal Chamber and Marilyn Manson among the other support acts. The Melvins run, July to October, was Helmet's last stretch of US shows before 2004. In late October and early November came seven shows in Australia and one in Auckland.

years.big: "9 years, 1,600 shows, 5 albums, and we found it hard to look at each other anymore."
years.h: The original run ends, officially, in November 1998
years.p: Hamilton's statement, as Wikipedia prints it. The last show was December 10, 1997 in Italy.

eras.title: A long quiet, with Bowie in it
eras.text: The members scatter: Hamilton to David Bowie's band, Stanier to Mike Patton's Tomahawk and then Battles.

years.h: Hamilton takes a guitar job with David Bowie
years.p: After the split he plays on Bowie's 1999 tour and writes film music with composer Elliot Goldenthal.
years.xp: He also played in a guitar orchestra, Deaf Elk, and kept a New York band called Gandhi, whose songs fed later Helmet records.

years.h: Stanier lands in Tomahawk, then Battles
years.p: The drummer joins [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]]'s Tomahawk, then [[Battles|8522b9b6-b295-48d7-9a10-8618fb80beb8]].

eras.title: Same name, new band, wrong label
eras.text: Hamilton revives Helmet as a working band with new players. Interscope drops it, and Warcon leaves him unpaid, he says.

years.h: Size Matters: new rhythm section, same name
years.p: Stanier and Bogdan decline to return, so John Tempesta plays drums and Chris Traynor bass. Out October 5.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the lyrics draw on Hamilton's brief 2003 relationship with actress Winona Ryder. The release slipped from September 14 after Hamilton broke his collarbone mountain biking. It debuted at No. 121 on the Billboard 200 with 9,723 copies in week one.

years.h: Interscope drops Helmet after Size Matters
years.p: Poor sales end the label relationship that began with the 1992 bidding war.

years.cap: Page Hamilton on stage at South by Southwest, March 2008
years.h: Hamilton says Warcon never paid for Monochrome
years.p: Recorded at Fun City with Wharton Tiers, on the same tape machine that made the first two albums. Hamilton says no royalties or tour support followed.
years.xp:
Out July 18, 2006 as a three-piece: Hamilton, Traynor and new drummer Mike Jost. Helmet had signed to Warcon that March. It sold 6,000 copies in its first week and peaked at No. 159. The title track went on the Saw III soundtrack with a video.

Hamilton later: "I trusted somebody and got screwed. I'm not bitter about it, but I lost a lot of money." He now owns the record.

years.h: Helmet fills in on the Guns N' Roses tour
years.p: The band opens the remaining December 2006 dates, after cancellations on the tour.

eras.title: Still touring
eras.text: The line-up settles, the albums keep coming, and the 1992 record gets played front to back in 2012.

years.cap: Page Hamilton at Sala Live, Madrid, February 2009
years.src: Wikipedia: Seeing Eye Dog · Wikipedia: Helmet (band) · Kerrang!: The great unsung
years.h: Seeing Eye Dog adds a Beatles cover and two new players
years.p: Out September 7 on Work Song, made in North Hollywood with producer Toshi Kasai. Kyle Stevenson plays drums and Beeman the second guitar.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 66, with Rock Sound at 9 of 10 and Spin at 5. Hamilton told Noisecreep the band's category was simple: "It's just Helmet."

Each of the five formats carried a bonus live disc from a July 8, 2006 show in San Francisco. Chris Traynor still played bass on the album; Dave Case is listed as bassist from 2010.

years.cap: Page Hamilton at Sala Caracol, Madrid, March 8, 2012
years.h: Helmet plays Meantime in full, 28 shows across Europe
years.p: The tour runs March 5 to April 8, 2012. Mengede steps back on stage for one show, in Brisbane.

years.cap: Helmet at Hellfest, Clisson, France, June 2017
years.src: Kerrang!: The great unsung · Wikipedia: Helmet (band)
years.h: Dead to the World arrives with Dave Case on bass
years.p: Released October 28, 2016, after the single "Bad News". The same year a hardcore tribute, Meantime Redux, appears.
years.xp: Kerrang! called it "possibly the finest record following the band's resurrection."

years.cap: Page Hamilton after the 30th anniversary show in Frankfurt, September 2019
years.h: Helmet turns 30 on the road
years.p: Anniversary tours cover Europe and North America in 2019, then New Zealand and Australia in 2020.

years.h: Seven years of quiet, then Left
years.p: "Holiday" leads in August; the album follows on November 10 on earMUSIC, with a John Coltrane cover to close it.
years.xp:
Hamilton and Kyle Stevenson wrote most of it; Hamilton produced with Jim Kaufman and Mark Renk. Two more singles followed, "Gun Fluf" on September 20 and "Big Shot" on October 18.

Reviews split: Distorted Sound gave it 8 of 10, Kerrang! 2 of 5.

years.h: The Local H tour is called off, then moved to 2025
years.p: A July 2024 US run with Local H, built around the Betty anniversary, is cancelled in August. A North American tour with Slomosa, War on Women and Effusion 35 takes its place in February and March 2025.

sources.title: Kerrang!: The great unsung heroics of Helmet, album by album
